title: Impact Evaluation Of The Mozambique Rural Water Supply Activity
evaluator: Virginia Tech, Stanford University and WE Consult
authority: The evaluation team worked with MCC and Mozambique’s Millennium Challenge Account. The original evaluation documents their respective roles.
scope: Rural water point installation in Nampula, a component of the Water Supply and Sanitation Project.
timing: The 2013 endline followed Phase 2 water-point installation. The final report was issued in August 2014.
method: Before-and-after comparison of 15 treatment and 23 comparison communities. The authors estimated a difference in differences.
summary: The estimated reduction in a round trip to the primary water source was 62 minutes relative to comparison communities (p < 0.05).
limitation: The measure is the mean of community median times. The study covered selected rural communities. Its estimates cannot be applied to the entire water project.
evidence: Original report, evaluation design and Table 7.14. The two declines are 85 and 23 minutes.

title: Impacts of a Large-Scale Agricultural Training Program in Armenia
evaluator: Randall Blair, Kenneth Fortson, Joanne Lee and Anu Rangarajan
authority: MCC lists the Water to Market farmer-training impact evaluation in its own evaluation catalogue (evaluations-armenia).
scope: Farmer training under Water to Market, within the irrigated agriculture project.
timing: Farmers were observed three years after training. The agency catalogues the 2007–2011 evaluation and the paper was published in 2020.
summary: Three years after training, the authors found no statistically detectable improvement in household income, consumption, higher-value crop cultivation or farming practices.
limitation: The available abstract gives no numerical effect sizes or confidence intervals. A statistically inconclusive estimate can include gains or losses.
evidence: MCC evaluation catalogue, evaluations-armenia, and 3ie record 13704, evaluators’ abstract.

title: An Impact Evaluation Of The MIDA FBO Training
evaluator: Institute of Statistical, Social and Economic Research, University of Ghana
authority: A participant-country research institution performed the evaluation. MCC lists the Commercial Training Activity impact evaluation in its catalogue (evaluations-ghana).
scope: Farmer-based organization training and starter packs.
timing: Follow-up interviews assessed trained farmers after their 27 contact days. Surveys ran from November 2008 to January 2011, while the wider compact was operating. The evaluation was published in 2012.
method: Randomized phase-in comparing early and late training groups.
summary: The evaluation found higher use of improved seeds and fertilizer, and no detectable overall increase in crop yields or crop income. Crop income effects differed by zone.
limitation: The study assessed short-run outcomes. Starter packs included seeds and fertilizer, which complicates interpretation of the input-use increase.
evidence: ISSER study abstract, 3ie record 5331, and MCC catalogue entry evaluations-ghana.

title: How Urban Land Titling and Registry Reform Affect Land and Credit Markets: Evidence from Lesotho
evaluator: Klaus Deininger and Daniel Ayalew Ali, World Bank
authority: 3ie identifies MCC as the research funder for the Lesotho Land Administration Reform Project study.
scope: Urban land titling and registry reform, within the Private Sector Development Project.
timing: The compact ended in 2013. The study follows registry activity through 2019 and reports medium-term outcomes.
method: Spatial fixed effects with time-varying controls, using land-registry data and satellite imagery.
summary: Titling helped women become registered co-owners. The authors attributed greater property-sale and mortgage activity to lower registration costs under a separate policy change.
limitation: The study separates two reforms that overlapped in time. Crediting all market activity to titling would overstate its effect.
evidence: 3ie record 23527, research funding field and evaluators’ abstract. MCC compact calendar for Lesotho.

title: Cooperation in the Commons: Community-based Rangeland Management in Namibia
authority: 3ie links the underlying evaluation to MCC’s official evaluation catalogue, study 138. The registered trial names the same implementer and intervention.
scope: Community-Based Rangeland and Livestock Management under the Agriculture Project.
timing: The trial registry records the end of the intervention in July 2014 and the end of the completed study in June 2017. The working paper appeared in 2021.
method: Randomized evaluation of communal grazing areas.
summary: Eight of thirteen social and behavioral indices improved. Effects on rangeland health, cattle productivity and household economic outcomes were negative or statistically indistinguishable from zero.
limitation: The abstract groups the ecological and economic findings. It does not state a separate estimate for each, and better management practices did not establish better household outcomes.
evidence: 3ie record 20118, primary dataset at data.mcc.gov/evaluations/index.php/catalog/138/study-description and AEA trial 2723.

title: The Impact Of Rural Business Services On The Economic Well-Being Of Small Farmers In Nicaragua
evaluator: Michael R. Carter, Patricia Toledo and Emilia Tjernström
authority: The published follow-up on this same randomized program (3ie 12695) lists MCC and USAID as research funders.
scope: Rural business development services for small farmers, a component of the Rural Development Project.
timing: The evaluation followed the five-year program through completion. The authors reported its results in 2012 and subsequently published post-program follow-up.
method: Randomized rollout and analysis by duration of participation.
summary: Income in the farm activities targeted by the program rose to about 30% above baseline after two years. The evaluators found no statistically significant average effect on household living standards.
limitation: The 30% refers to targeted farm activities relative to baseline. It does not measure total household income or a 30% reduction in poverty.
evidence: 3ie record 6337, evaluators’ abstract. Research sponsors are identified in follow-up record 12695.

title: Heterogeneous Impact Dynamics Of A Rural Business Development Program In Nicaragua
authority: 3ie identifies MCC and USAID as research funders.
scope: Follow-up on the same rural business development intervention reported in 2012.
timing: The authors explicitly report effects persisting after the program concluded.
method: Randomized treatment assignment, with analysis by exposure duration and household characteristics.
summary: Gross farm income gains persisted and productive farm capital continued to rise after completion. Some households benefited little.
limitation: This paper follows the same intervention and population as the earlier report. The available abstract does not quantify the persistent average gain.
evidence: 3ie record 12695, research funding and evaluators’ abstract.

title: The Medium-Term Impacts Of Girl-Friendly Schools: Seven-Year Evidence From School Construction In Burkina Faso
evaluator: Harounan Kazianga, Leigh Linden, Ali Protik and Matt Sloan
authority: The study identifies the Burkinabè Ministry of Education as implementer and MCC and the national government as program funders. The accessible record does not identify the commissioner of this research.
scope: BRIGHT school expansion, including the second phase.
timing: The study measures outcomes six years into the intervention after schools were upgraded from three classrooms to six.
method: Regression discontinuity comparing villages on either side of the selection threshold.
summary: Enrollment was 15.5 percentage points higher and test scores were 0.29 standard deviations higher. The estimates cover exposure to the phased BRIGHT program.
limitation: An incremental Phase 2 effect cannot be isolated from the reported overall estimates. The research sponsor could not be verified.
evidence: 3ie record 8060, evaluators’ abstract, named implementing agency and program funding fields.

title: The Long-Term Impacts of Girl-Friendly Schools: Evidence from the BRIGHT School Construction Program in Burkina Faso
authority: 3ie lists the U.S. National Institute of Child Health and Human Development as a research funder. Direct commissioning by MCC, USAID or the Burkina Faso government was unverified.
scope: Ten-year follow-up in villages selected for the two-phase BRIGHT school program.
timing: Primary-school-age children, older youths and young adults were assessed ten years after the program began.
method: Regression discontinuity around the village selection threshold.
summary: Children in selected villages attended school more and scored higher on tests. Among women old enough to have completed secondary school, marriage and childbearing occurred later.
limitation: Findings refer to the phased program in selected villages. The available abstract does not isolate the contribution of Phase 2.
evidence: 3ie record 19120, research funder and evaluators’ abstract.

title: Formalizing Rural Land Rights In West Africa: Early Evidence From A Randomized Impact Evaluation In Benin
authority: 3ie lists World Bank, Belgian, French and UN research funding. Direct commissioning by the Beninese government or MCC was unverified.
scope: Village-level land demarcation within the Plan Foncier Rural.
timing: The authors examined treated parcels after boundary demarcation and before the completion of certification.
method: Randomized comparison of villages offered land demarcation.
summary: Treated parcels saw a shift toward longer-term investment. The study found no accompanying increase in agricultural productivity at this early follow-up.
limitation: The paper reports an early stage in land formalization. It cannot establish the long-term productivity effect of receiving a certificate.
evidence: 3ie record 6163, program identity, research funders and evaluators’ abstract.
